problem: Continuous VLN (VLN-CE) agents only use word-level instruction features, suffering from noise-word attention and word-grouping problems. Prior sub-instruction methods (FGR2R, SpC-NAV) are slow, designed for discrete settings, and still use only word features within a sub-instruction.
motivation: Continuous VLN demands real-time execution, complex instruction understanding and long action sequence prediction. Humans split instructions into sub-goals; injecting sub-instruction (high-level) semantics alongside word (low-level) semantics should reduce noise-word effects and give more precise action guidance.
key_idea: Segment instructions into sub-instructions with a fast annotation-free algorithm, fuse word-level and sub-instruction-level features with multi-head attention (MLA), and sharpen sub-instruction attention into a single peak with an auxiliary loss (PAL).
insight: Ablations on val-unseen (imitation only) show every part matters: removing FSA, MLA or PAL drops SPL from 0.21 to 0.19, 0.19 and 0.18 respectively, so sub-instruction features, multi-level fusion and attention shaping all contribute. The Gaussian PAL curve beats constant/linear/quadratic/cubic curves, and sigma=0.6 balances seen/unseen, whereas sigma=0.8 overfits to seen. FSA is roughly as good as the heavy FGR2R chunker for downstream SR/SPL while being about 70x faster.
method: Fast Sub-instruction Algorithm (FSA): cleans text, splits with a coarse sentence tokenizer, then refines boundaries with heuristic rules on POS tags; annotation-free, plug-and-play; produces the FSASub dataset (7.3 min vs 8.8 h for the FGR2R chunker)
Encoders: CLIP ViT-B/32 RGB encoder, ResNet depth encoder, BiLSTM word encoder (low-level), CLIP text Transformer sub-instruction encoder (high-level)

Multi-Level Attention (MLA): two GRU vision memories (h^h, h^l) act as queries to multi-head attention over sub-instruction features and word features respectively; the outputs are concatenated and passed through an FC layer to give the fused instruction feature (512-d, 8 heads)

Peak Attention Loss (PAL): MSE between the high-level attention score and a Gaussian-like target peaked at the argmax sub-instruction (sigma=0.6), no gradient through argmax; lambda linearly ramped 0 to 0.4
Action decoder: GRU over concatenated states, instruction and spatial-attended visual features, giving softmax over 4 actions; loss = action CE + lambda*PAL + theta*progress monitor
Training: imitation learning, with DAgger, EnvDrop-style augmentation and PPO fine-tuning for the best model

setting.backbone: CLIP ViT-B/32 RGB + CLIP text Transformer + ResNet depth + BiLSTM + GRU decoder (trained end-to-end, CLIP encoders pretrained)
setting.training_data: VLN-CE R2R train (with FSASub sub-instructions), DAgger, EnvDrop augmentation data, then PPO fine-tuning

results: On the VLN-CE test leaderboard MLANet reaches SR 0.34 and SPL 0.32, beating HPN+DN (0.32 / 0.30) and CMA (0.28 / 0.25), though its NE (6.78) is worse than HPN+DN (6.65). On val-unseen the full model gets SPL 0.35 vs 0.20-0.23 for Seq2Seq/CMA under the same training.
limitations: Simple RNN-based framework may limit use of sub-instructions and observations; a Transformer is suggested
Sensitive to uncommon words or observations (e.g., rare objects, long hallways), giving oscillating or stuck attention
Baselines could not be RL fine-tuned equally, and ablations are only under imitation learning
